title: Composing with it
description: For writing a piece: teach it a direction, breed and keep a palette, put timbre and arpeggios on the tempo, record takes, and carry the sounds with you.

lines.text: A piece needs a palette, like a bass, a pad and a moving texture.
Here is how to grow one.
First, point it. The warm start shows nine presets.
Pick the three nearest your piece. That is eighteen answers in thirty seconds.
Then answer duels, fast. A gut reaction is the data.
Press Evolve Pool, and it breeds from the ten patches it rates highest.
The children resemble their parents, bent toward what you chose.
The weakest leave the pool, and anything you saved stays.
When a sound fits the piece, save it to My Patches.
A saved patch is never replaced, up to a quarter of the pool.
Stars are opinions, and they teach. Then name the sound for its part.
For movement, put Steps on a filter.
You draw up to eight bars, and the timbre plays them as a pattern.
Turn on Sync, and the pattern snaps to the nearest division of the tempo.
It restarts with your first key.
The arpeggiator runs at the same tempo.
Latch a chord with Hold, and the line plays itself while you shape the sound.
Send MIDI clock from your sequencer, and both follow its tempo.
A MIDI start brings the sequencers and the arpeggiator in on its downbeat.
Inside a part, Keep marks a sound as home, and Back glides the knobs home again.
Between parts, step through My Patches with the bracket keys.
Held notes carry across the change without a click.
Press record, play the part, and press stop.
The take downloads as a WAV file, the instrument's own output after its limiter.
To keep a sound with the piece, export it as a patch file.
Or export a picture of the rack, with the patch inside it.
Drop either onto Auracle, and it opens as the same patch.
Everything autosaves in your browser. Before you move machines, save your taste profile too.
